projects.description:
# PROJECT: New SDLC Project

## EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
A high-fidelity, browser-based side-scrolling platformer inspired by the 8-bit classic Super Mario Bros. This project leverages HTML5 Canvas for hardware-accelerated rendering and the Web Audio API for procedural sound synthesis (eliminating heavy asset dependencies). The architecture separates the game loop, physics engine, and rendering logic to ensure smooth 60fps performance. It features a custom tile-based collision system, dynamic camera scrolling, entity management (enemies, particles, items), and responsive controls. The design utilizes a retro-modern aesthetic, combining pixel-perfect mechanics with modern UI overlays built via Tailwind CSS.

## TECH STACK
- HTML5 Canvas API
- Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+)
- Web Audio API (Procedural Sound Synthesis)
- Tailwind CSS (UI Overlay)
- Font Awesome (Icons)
- Local Storage API (High Score Persistence)

## DESIGN THEME
Sunset (Theme ID: sunset)

## ARCHITECTURE DIAGRAM
```mermaid
C4Container
    title Container Diagram for Browser-Based Platformer Game

    Person(user, "Player", "Plays the game via web browser")
    
    Container_Boundary(game_system, "Game System") {
        Container(browser_app, "SPA Game Client", "HTML5/JS", "The playable game application")
        
        Container_Component(game_loop, "Game Loop", "JS (rAF)", "Orchestrates updates and rendering 60 times/sec")
        Container_Component(physics, "Physics Engine", "JS", "Handles AABB collision, gravity, velocity")
        Container_Component(input, "Input Handler", "JS Event Listeners", "Captures keyboard/touch inputs")
        Container_Component(level_mgr, "Level Manager", "JS Class", "Parses map strings into renderable tiles")
        Container_Component(audio, "Audio Manager", "Web Audio API", "Synthesizes SFX procedurally")
        Container_Component(renderer, "Renderer", "Canvas API 2D", "Draws entities and UI to screen")
    }

    Rel(user, browser_app, "Interacts with", "HTTPS")
    Rel(browser_app, game_loop, "Starts")
    Rel(game_loop, physics, "Updates state")
    Rel(game_loop, renderer, "Triggers draw")
    Rel(input, game_loop, "Modifies state")
    Rel(physics, level_mgr, "Checks collision")
    Rel(game_loop, audio, "Triggers SFX")
```

## UI PROTOTYPE
(See 'Wireframe Prototype.html' artifact for the visual mockups. Agents should refer to this artifact for UI tasks.)

## IDENTIFIED RISKS
- **Performance on Low-End Mobile Devices**: The HTML5 Canvas drawing loop (60fps) coupled with constant collision detection checks against a large array of tiles may cause frame drops on older phones or aggressive power-saving modes.
- **Tunneling (Physics Engine)**: At high velocities or low frame rates, the simple AABB (Axis-Aligned Bounding Box) collision logic might allow the player to pass through thin walls or floors (tunneling effect).
- **Input Latency**: Touch controls on mobile browsers often introduce slight delays or 'ghost clicks' compared to hardware keyboards, potentially impacting the precision platforming experience.

artifacts.content:
# PROJECT CHARTER: HTML5 PLATFORMER INITIATIVE

| Project ID | `PRJ-PLAT-001` |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Project Name** | **Project: 8-BIT RESURGENCE** |
| **Orchestrator** | Raed |
| **Date** | October 26, 2023 |
| **Methodology** | Agile / Iterative |

---

## 1. MISSION STATEMENT
To engineer a high-fidelity, hardware-accelerated HTML5 side-scrolling platformer that replicates the precision mechanics of 8-bit classics. The system will prioritize zero-latency inputs, 60fps stability on standard viewports, and a dependency-free architecture using procedural audio and canvas rendering.

## 2. PROJECT OBJECTIVES
1.  **Core Performance:** Achieve a stable 60 frames-per-second (FPS) render loop via `requestAnimationFrame` on desktop and mid-tier mobile devices.
2.  **Asset Independence:** Eliminate reliance on external bitmap assets or audio files by utilizing Canvas API primitives and Web Audio API oscillators.
3.  **Persistence:** Implement a local-first high-score system using the browser's Local Storage API.
4.  **Responsiveness:** Deliver a fully responsive UI overlay (Tailwind CSS) that adapts to the "Sunset" thematic directive.

## 3. SCOPE DEFINITION

### 3.1 In-Scope (Critical Path)
*   **Game Loop Architecture:** Implementation of a detached update/draw loop structure.
*   **Physics Engine:** Custom AABB (Axis-Aligned Bounding Box) collision detection with gravity and velocity vectors.
*   **Level Management:** String/Array-based map parsing for tile generation.
*   **Audio Synthesis:** Procedural generation of Jump, Die, and Coin collection SFX.
*   **UI/HUD:** Score, Lives, and Game Over states overlayed via DOM elements.
*   **Input Handling:** Keyboard (Desktop) and Touch Zone (Mobile) event mapping.

### 3.2 Out-of-Scope (De-scoped)
*   Multiplayer or WebSocket integration.
*   Server-side databases or user authentication.
*   WebGL or 3D rendering contexts (Strict 2D Canvas only).
*   External gamepad API support (Keyboard/Touch only for MVP).

## 4. KEY DELIVERABLES & MILESTONES

| ID | Milestone | Description | Priority |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **M-01** | **The Skeleton** | Setup of HTML5 Canvas, Game Loop, and "Sunset" UI Shell. | P0 (Critical) |
| **M-02** | **Physics Core** | Implementation of gravity, velocity, and basic floor collision. | P0 (Critical) |
| **M-03** | **World Builder** | Level parsing logic and camera scrolling mechanics. | P1 |
| **M-04** | **Entity Logic** | Player state machine (Idle, Run, Jump) and Enemy AI (Patrol). | P1 |
| **M-05** | **Polish & Audio** | Procedural SFX integration and particle effects. | P2 |

## 5. TECHNICAL CONSTRAINTS & STANDARDS
*   **Codebase:** Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+). No heavy frameworks (React/Vue/Angular) allowed for the Game Logic to minimize overhead.
*   **Styling:** Tailwind CSS via CDN for UI overlays.
*   **Global State:** Minimal global scope pollution; use modular classes (`Game`, `Entity`, `Level`).
*   **Resolution:** Dynamic canvas sizing with aspect ratio maintenance.

## 6. RISK MITIGATION PLAN

| Risk ID | Risk Description | Probability | Impact | Mitigation Strategy |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **R-01** | **Physics Tunneling** | Medium | High | Implement **sub-stepping** or swept-collision checks for high-velocity entities to prevent passing through solid tiles. |
| **R-02** | **Mobile Performance** | High | Medium | Enforce **Object Pooling** for particles/projectiles to reduce Garbage Collection pauses. Limit draw calls per frame. |
| **R-03** | **Input Latency** | Medium | High | Decouple rendering from logic updates (Delta Time). Use specific touch event listeners (`touchstart` vs `click`) to remove 300ms mobile delay. |

## 7. STAKEHOLDERS
*   **Project Sponsor:** User
*   **Lead Orchestrator:** Raed (Architecture & Risk Mgmt)
*   **Development Unit:** AI Agents (Implementation)

---
**AUTHORIZATION**
*This charter defines the boundaries of the initiative. Deviation requires specific Orchestrator approval.*

**Status:** APPROVED FOR EXECUTION

As Sherif, I will conduct a Zero-Trust Regulatory & Compliance Check on the "New SDLC Project," a browser-based platformer game. My primary objective is to ensure absolute compliance with global standards, specifically ISO (principles), GDPR, and HIPAA, and to identify potential vulnerabilities related to data privacy and accessibility (WCAG).

My approach will involve a systematic review of the provided project context, focusing on the "Local Storage API (High Score Persistence)" for data privacy and the "HTML5 Canvas" and "Tailwind CSS (UI Overlay)" for accessibility.

**1. Data Privacy Review (GDPR & ISO Principles):**
*   **Identify Data Stored:** The Executive Summary explicitly mentions "Local Storage API (High Score Persistence)."
*   **GDPR Applicability Assessment:**
    *   Determine if the "high score" constitutes "personal data" under GDPR. If it's purely an anonymous numeric value, GDPR may not apply to the score itself. However, if any user identifier (e.g., username, unique device ID, IP address) is stored alongside the score, or if the score can be linked back to an individual, then GDPR provisions become highly relevant.
    *   **Key GDPR Considerations if Personal Data is Present:** Lawfulness (consent/legitimate interest), purpose limitation, data minimization, accuracy, storage limitation, integrity and confidentiality (security), and accountability. Crucially, the "Right to Erasure" and "Right to Access" must be enabled for users.
*   **ISO Principles Applicability (Information Security):** Even if not personal data, the integrity of high scores (preventing tampering) and general data security practices are relevant under ISO 27001 principles.
*   **Formulate Recommendations:** Based on the assessment, provide clear recommendations for handling high score data, particularly concerning user identification, consent, and user rights.

**2. HIPAA Applicability Review:**
*   **Assess Project Scope:** Evaluate if the project's nature (a "super mario game") involves any Protected Health Information (PHI).
*   **Formulate Conclusion:** State definitively whether HIPAA is applicable or not.

**3. Accessibility Review (WCAG):**
*   **Identify Relevant Components:** HTML5 Canvas (game rendering), Tailwind CSS (UI Overlay), and overall user interaction (controls).
*   **WCAG Principles (Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, Robust) Assessment:**
    *   **Perceivable:**
        *   **Color Contrast:** For UI overlays (Tailwind CSS), ensure sufficient contrast ratios for text and graphical components (WCAG AA/AAA).
        *   **Non-text Content Alternatives:** Consider if critical game information conveyed solely visually on the Canvas needs text alternatives for screen reader users (e.g., game state, essential notifications).
        *   **Audio:** Since Web Audio API is used for procedural synthesis, ensure any essential audio cues have visual alternatives or captions if they convey critical information without visual counterparts.
        *   **No Flashing Content:** Verify the game does not contain any content that flashes more than three times per second, which could induce seizures.
    *   **Operable:**
        *   **Keyboard Navigation:** All interactive UI elements (menus, buttons) built with Tailwind CSS must be keyboard focusable and operable. The core gameplay itself must also be fully playable via keyboard.
        *   **Input Modalities:** Ensure the game supports various input methods beyond just mouse/touch for UI, and provides options for remapping controls if possible.
        *   **Time Limits:** If any game sections have time limits, ensure they are reasonable or can be adjusted.
    *   **Understandable:**
        *   **Readability:** Ensure UI text (Tailwind) is readable, clear, and uses consistent language.
        *   **Predictability:** UI navigation and game mechanics should be predictable.
    *   **Robust:**
        *   Ensure compatibility with common assistive technologies. Standard HTML/CSS for UI is generally robust, but Canvas content requires careful consideration.
*   **Formulate Recommendations:** Provide specific, actionable recommendations for enhancing accessibility, focusing on both the UI overlays and the core game experience.

**Execution Plan:**
1.  Draft the review report, addressing each standard sequentially.
2.  Clearly state findings and provide prioritized recommendations.
3.  Ensure the language is precise, professional, and adheres to zero-trust principles, leaving no ambiguity.

artifacts.content:
# PROJECT CHARTER: HTML5 PLATFORMER INITIATIVE

| Project ID | `PRJ-PLAT-001` |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Project Name** | **Project: 8-BIT RESURGENCE** |
| **Orchestrator** | Raed |
| **Date** | October 26, 2023 |
| **Methodology** | Agile / Iterative |

---

## 1. MISSION STATEMENT
To engineer a high-fidelity, hardware-accelerated HTML5 side-scrolling platformer that replicates the precision mechanics of 8-bit classics. The system will prioritize zero-latency inputs, 60fps stability on standard viewports, and a dependency-free architecture using procedural audio and canvas rendering.

## 2. PROJECT OBJECTIVES
1.  **Core Performance:** Achieve a stable 60 frames-per-second (FPS) render loop via `requestAnimationFrame` on desktop and mid-tier mobile devices.
2.  **Asset Independence:** Eliminate reliance on external bitmap assets or audio files by utilizing Canvas API primitives and Web Audio API oscillators.
3.  **Persistence:** Implement a local-first high-score system using the browser's Local Storage API.
4.  **Responsiveness:** Deliver a fully responsive UI overlay (Tailwind CSS) that adapts to the "Sunset" thematic directive.

## 3. SCOPE DEFINITION

### 3.1 In-Scope (Critical Path)
*   **Game Loop Architecture:** Implementation of a detached update/draw loop structure.
*   **Physics Engine:** Custom AABB (Axis-Aligned Bounding Box) collision detection with gravity and velocity vectors.
*   **Level Management:** String/Array-based map parsing for tile generation.
*   **Audio Synthesis:** Procedural generation of Jump, Die, and Coin collection SFX.
*   **UI/HUD:** Score, Lives, and Game Over states overlayed via DOM elements.
*   **Input Handling:** Keyboard (Desktop) and Touch Zone (Mobile) event mapping.

### 3.2 Out-of-Scope (De-scoped)
*   Multiplayer or WebSocket integration.
*   Server-side databases or user authentication.
*   WebGL or 3D rendering contexts (Strict 2D Canvas only).
*   External gamepad API support (Keyboard/Touch only for MVP).

## 4. KEY DELIVERABLES & MILESTONES

| ID | Milestone | Description | Priority |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **M-01** | **The Skeleton** | Setup of HTML5 Canvas, Game Loop, and "Sunset" UI Shell. | P0 (Critical) |
| **M-02** | **Physics Core** | Implementation of gravity, velocity, and basic floor collision. | P0 (Critical) |
| **M-03** | **World Builder** | Level parsing logic and camera scrolling mechanics. | P1 |
| **M-04** | **Entity Logic** | Player state machine (Idle, Run, Jump) and Enemy AI (Patrol). | P1 |
| **M-05** | **Polish & Audio** | Procedural SFX integration and particle effects. | P2 |

## 5. TECHNICAL CONSTRAINTS & STANDARDS
*   **Codebase:** Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+). No heavy frameworks (React/Vue/Angular) allowed for the Game Logic to minimize overhead.
*   **Styling:** Tailwind CSS via CDN for UI overlays.
*   **Global State:** Minimal global scope pollution; use modular classes (`Game`, `Entity`, `Level`).
*   **Resolution:** Dynamic canvas sizing with aspect ratio maintenance.

## 6. RISK MITIGATION PLAN

| Risk ID | Risk Description | Probability | Impact | Mitigation Strategy |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **R-01** | **Physics Tunneling** | Medium | High | Implement **sub-stepping** or swept-collision checks for high-velocity entities to prevent passing through solid tiles. |
| **R-02** | **Mobile Performance** | High | Medium | Enforce **Object Pooling** for particles/projectiles to reduce Garbage Collection pauses. Limit draw calls per frame. |
| **R-03** | **Input Latency** | Medium | High | Decouple rendering from logic updates (Delta Time). Use specific touch event listeners (`touchstart` vs `click`) to remove 300ms mobile delay. |

## 7. STAKEHOLDERS
*   **Project Sponsor:** User
*   **Lead Orchestrator:** Raed (Architecture & Risk Mgmt)
*   **Development Unit:** AI Agents (Implementation)

---

tasks.description: Document the primary game loop, player controls, and core interactive elements (e.g., platforming physics, shooting, collecting) to guide technical design.

tasks.description: Outline the high-level architecture, specifying the use of raw HTML5 Canvas API vs. wrappers, ECMAScript version, and module structure.

tasks.description: Establish the visual language of the game, deciding between pixel art or vector graphics, color palettes, and overall aesthetic mood.

tasks.title: Game Loop and Time Step Design
tasks.description: Design the main game loop logic using requestAnimationFrame, ensuring independent update and render cycles to handle variable frame rates.

tasks.title: Physics Engine Specification
tasks.description: Define the mathematical model for gravity, velocity, and friction. Determine if a custom implementation or a lightweight library is required.

tasks.title: Sprite Asset Requirements List
tasks.description: Create a detailed list of all required animations (idle, run, jump, attack) for the main character and enemies.

tasks.title: Collision Detection Strategy
tasks.description: Select the appropriate collision algorithms (AABB for tiles, circle collision for particles) and design the spatial partitioning system (e.g., Quadtree) for performance.

tasks.title: HUD and UI Wireframes
tasks.description: Create wireframes for the Heads-Up Display (score, health, ammo) and main menu screens to ensure optimal user experience.

tasks.title: Level Progression Logic
tasks.description: Define how levels advance, including difficulty scaling, unlock criteria, and data persistence between stages.

tasks.title: Input Handling System Design
tasks.description: Design an event-driven input manager to abstract keyboard and mouse events into game actions, supporting remappable controls.

tasks.title: Power-up Mechanics Definition
tasks.description: Specify the types of power-ups available, their duration, visual feedback, and impact on game physics or player stats.

tasks.title: Audio Requirements Specification
tasks.description: List all necessary sound effects (jump, hit, explosion) and background music tracks needed for different game states.

tasks.title: Browser Compatibility Matrix
tasks.description: Define the target browsers and devices, establishing performance budgets for canvas rendering and memory usage.

tasks.title: Game State Management Design
tasks.description: Architect the state machine to handle transitions between Loading, Menu, Playing, Paused, and Game Over states.

tasks.title: Character Concept Art
tasks.description: Draft initial character sketches based on the visual style guide and asset requirements list.

tasks.title: Scoring and High Score System Specs
tasks.description: Detail the formula for calculating scores, combo multipliers, and the local storage structure for saving high scores.

tasks.title: Repository Setup and Directory Structure
tasks.description: Create the git repository and establish the folder structure (assets, src, css, index.html) according to the architecture plan.

tasks.title: Initial Test Plan Strategy
tasks.description: Draft a plan for testing physics edge cases, collision accuracy, and frame rate stability across defined browsers.

tasks.title: Initiation Phase Gate Review
tasks.description: Audit all generated requirements, designs, and architectural documents to ensure readiness for the Implementation phase.

faqs.question: How does OrbitAI differ from other AI coding assistants?
faqs.answer: OrbitAI uses a multi-agent orchestration system with strict V-Model SDLC enforcement, automated risk assessment, and scope control. It's not just code generation - it's a complete software development lifecycle management system.

faqs.question: What is the V-Model SDLC?
faqs.answer: The V-Model is a software development methodology that emphasizes verification and validation at each phase. OrbitAI enforces this model to ensure quality and reduce risk throughout development.

faqs.question: Can I use OrbitAI for any programming language?
faqs.answer: OrbitAI supports multiple programming languages and frameworks. The agents adapt to your project's tech stack and requirements.

faqs.question: How does risk assessment work?
faqs.answer: Our Risk Assessment Agent analyzes your project requirements, identifies potential risks, and suggests mitigation strategies before development begins.

faqs.question: Is my code secure?
faqs.answer: Yes. OrbitAI runs in isolated environments and never stores your code without explicit permission. All data is encrypted and secure.
